description: Jointed sensory appendage of the head: scape, pedicel and 14 flagellomeres (fI–fXIV). Older keys number the segments from the scape, so antenna 3 = fI, antenna 4 = fII, antenna 5 = fIII.
First (basal) segment of the antenna, short and cup-shaped.
Second segment of the antenna, globular, between the scape and the first flagellomere.
The first long antennal segment after scape and pedicel = 'antenna 3' (A3, AIII) of older keys. Its length, often compared with the labrum, is used in many couplets.
= 'antenna 4' of older keys. Ascoid length is often expressed relative to it (asc/f2).
The last four flagellomeres, shorter than the basal ones. Presence of ascoids and papillae on them is used in some keys.
Ratio of the length of the ascoid to the length of flagellomere 2 (antenna 4).
Length of flagellomere 1 (antenna 3) divided by the length of the labrum-epipharynx (E). A value below 1 means antenna 3 is shorter than the labrum.
Five-segmented sensory appendage beside the proboscis (p1–p5). The order of the segments by length gives the palpal formula, e.g. 1-2-4-3-5.
Basal segment of the palp, usually the shortest.
Second segment of the palp.
Third segment of the palp; carries the Newstead's sensilla.
Fourth segment of the palp, often short.
Distal segment of the palp, usually the longest; whether it is the longest is used in some keys.
Large compound eye on each side of the head. Its size and the distance between the eyes (interocular distance) are measured in descriptions.
Narrowest distance between the two compound eyes across the frons.
Sclerite on the front of the head between the antennae, above the base of the labrum.
Measurement: length of the head from the vertex to the lower edge of the clypeus.
Measurement: greatest width of the head across the eyes.
Measurement: greatest length of the compound eye.
Measurement: width of the compound eye.
Measurement: length of the clypeus.
Measurement: length of flagellomere 1 (antenna 3), compared with the labrum or other segments in many keys.
Measurement: total length of the palp (p1–p5).
Upper blade of the proboscis; its length (E) is the standard for comparing antenna 3 and palpal segments.
Paired blade-like mouthparts with fine teeth, used by females to cut the skin.
Median blade of the proboscis that carries the salivary channel.
Lower lip that sheathes the other mouthparts and ends in two labella.
Blade of the maxilla, toothed at the tip in blood-feeding females.
Muscular tube behind the cibarium; its shape and armature are diagnostic.
Teeth, spines or ridges on the posterior part of the pharynx (pharyngeal armature).
Chamber at the base of the mouthparts, in front of the pharynx, that carries the cibarial armature.
Row of large horizontal teeth at the back of the cibarium ('hind teeth' of older keys).
Small vertical teeth in front of the posterior teeth ('fore teeth' of older keys).
Teeth at the sides of the cibarium, outside the main row.
Projection at the back of the cibarium, near the posterior bridge.
Sclerotized bridge at the junction of cibarium and pharynx.
Chitinous arch crossing the cibarium; complete or incomplete in different groups.
Pigmented (sclerotized) patch in the middle of the cibarium; its shape and colour are used in keys.
Sclerotized strip along each side of the cibarium.
The five branches of the radius, numbered from the front margin of the wing.
The four branches of the media, behind the radial veins.
Short cross-vein joining radius and media near the wing base.
Wing index α: length of vein R2 from its fork to the wing margin.
Wing index β: length of the stem R2+3, from the fork of R2+3+4 to the fork of R2 and R3. Keys use the ratio α/β (R2/R2+3).
Wing index γ: length of the stem R2+3+4, from the r-m cross-vein to its fork.
Wing index δ: distance between the tip of R1 and the fork of R2+3; positive when R1 ends beyond the fork.
Wing index ε: length of vein R3.
Wing index θ: length of vein R4 from the fork of R2+3+4 to the wing margin.
Wing index π: distance between the fork of R2+3+4 and the fork of M1+2.
Second branch of the radius; its length is wing index α.
Measurement: from the wing base to the tip.
Measurement: greatest width of the wing.
Dorsal plate of an abdominal segment (numbered 1st–10th).
Ventral plate of an abdominal segment.
Paired terminal appendage at the tip of the abdomen, above the 10th sternite.
Small knob at the apex of the spermatheca, often set in a neck; its shape is used in keys.
Duct leading from each spermatheca; joins its partner to form the common duct.
Short duct formed by the union of the two individual ducts.
Median stem of the genital furca (genital fork).
Fork-shaped sclerite of the 9th segment in females, supporting the genital opening.
Small appendage of the 8th segment in females (8th gonopod).
Sclerotized area of the 8th segment near the genital opening in females.
Distal segment of the male clasper, carrying the large spines.
Basal segment of the male clasper.
Paired median appendage of the male genitalia, often with setae and lobes.
Sclerotized sheath around the end of the aedeagal ducts.
Paired ducts from the sperm pump to the tip of the parameral sheath; their length and tip shape are diagnostic.
Bulb-shaped pump inside the abdomen that pushes sperm along the aedeagal ducts.
Rod-like apodeme attached to the sperm pump.
Paired lateral lobe below the clasper ('surstyle' or 'lateral lobe' of older keys).
Large spines of the gonostyle. Their number and position (apical, upper and lower external, internal) are key characters for subgenera.
Ventral plate of the 9th segment of the male.
Dorsal plate of the 10th segment of the male.
Ventral plate of the 10th segment of the male.
Transverse fold (ridge) of the pharynx wall, seen in the posterior part of the pharynx.
Hyaline sensory rod (geniculated spine) on a flagellomere; the number per flagellomere gives the ascoidal (antennal) formula.
The inner of the two ascoids on a flagellomere; its position on fI is recorded in descriptions.
Papilla at the tip of a flagellomere.
Papilla just before the tip of a flagellomere.
Papilla in the middle of a flagellomere.
Papilla near the base of a flagellomere.
Papilla just before (basal to) the ascoid.
Spine-shaped papilla on an apical flagellomere.
Ordinary hair (seta) on a flagellomere or palpal segment; position and number are recorded in descriptions.
= 'antenna 5' of older keys; papillae on fIII separate some species (e.g. P. argentipes and P. philippinensis).
Club-shaped sensilla on the palp, usually grouped on p3.
Sclerite of the side (pleuron) of the thorax, behind the upper and lower anepisternum. Bears the anepimeral setae, or scales in Grassomyia.
Front part of the pronotum, behind the neck.
Breathing opening (spiracle) on the front of the thorax. Not to be confused with as = ascoid on the antenna.
Sclerite below the postnotum at the back of the thorax.
Sclerite of the neck (cervix), with a pair of sensilla.
Knob-like hind wing used for balance in flight.
Lower sclerite of the pleuron behind the katepisternum.
Large lower sclerite of the side of the thorax, above the middle leg.
Small sclerite below the postnotum, near the posterior spiracle.
Lower part of the anepisternum, in front of the anepimeron; may bear lower anepisternal setae.
Dorsal sclerite of the third thoracic segment; may bear metanotal setae.
Coxa (first leg segment) of the middle leg.
Internal fork-shaped apodeme of the mesothorax.
Coxa of the hind leg.
Internal fork-shaped apodeme of the metathorax; whether its vertical arms are united or separate is recorded in descriptions.
Posterior pleural sclerite of the metathorax; may bear metepimeral setae.
Anterior pleural sclerite of the metathorax; may bear metepisternal setae.
Posterior pleural sclerite of the prothorax; may bear proepimeral setae.
Anterior pleural sclerite of the prothorax.
Hind part of the mesonotum, behind the scutellum.
Hind part of the pronotum.
Projection of the prosternum between the front legs.
Coxa of the front leg.
Internal fork-shaped apodeme of the prothorax.
Breathing opening at the back of the thorax.
Front part of the mesonotum; may bear prescutal setae.
Small sclerite at the side of the mesonotum; may bear paratergital setae.
Rounded sclerite at the back of the mesonotum; bears scutellar setae.
Main dorsal plate of the mesothorax.
Upper part of the anepisternum; may bear upper anepisternal setae.
Sclerite on the underside of the neck; may bear ventrocervical sensilla.
Base of the wing.
Setae on the anepimeron; their presence or absence is recorded in descriptions.
Setae in rows along the middle of the scutum.
Setae on the lower anepisternum (presence or absence recorded).
Setae on the metanotum.
Setae on the metepimeron (presence or absence recorded).
Setae on the metepisternum (presence and number recorded).
Setae on the proepimeron (presence or absence recorded).
Setae on the prescutum.
Setae on the scutum behind the transverse suture.
Setae above the wing base.
Setae on the scutellum.
Setae on the upper anepisternum (presence or absence recorded).
Sensilla on the ventrocervical sclerite (presence or absence recorded).
